questions.question: In an assignment problem with unequal numbers of agents and tasks, what is a dummy assignment?
options: Removing surplus agents or tasks until the numbers are equal
Adding fictitious agents or tasks at cost 0 to square the table
Giving surplus agents a second task so that every task is covered
Adding fictitious agents or tasks with a very large cost

questions.question: An assignment problem has 3 agents (rows) and 5 tasks (columns), with costs $c_{ij}$. Which addition makes the cost table square?
options: Two dummy task columns with all costs 0
One dummy agent row that takes two tasks
Two dummy agent rows with all costs 0
Two dummy agent rows with each task's largest cost

questions.question: After a dummy task column with zero costs is added to an assignment table with more agents than tasks, a real agent is assigned to the dummy task. What does this mean?
options: The agent stays unused and performs no real task
The agent performs a real task at no cost
The agent shares a real task with another agent
The solution is infeasible for the original problem

questions.question: A firm has fewer agents than tasks, so its cost table gets a fictitious agent whose costs are all 0. In the optimal square solution this fictitious agent receives task $T_2$. How should this be read?
options: Task $T_2$ is left unperformed
Task $T_2$ is performed for free
Task $T_2$ is shared among the real agents
Task $T_2$ is the most expensive task

questions.question: When a rectangular assignment problem is made square with dummy rows or columns, why are the dummy costs set to 0?
options: Zero costs stop the model from choosing any dummy entries
Zero costs are needed to make the cost table square
Zero costs make every real agent equally likely to stay idle
An unused agent or unfilled task is assumed to cost nothing

questions.question: Agents $A_1,A_2,A_3$ and tasks $T_1,T_2$ have costs $A_1$: 7, 4; $A_2$: 5, 8; $A_3$: 6, 3 (for $T_1$, $T_2$). Each task needs one agent and each agent does at most one task, so a dummy task with zero costs is added. Which assignment minimizes total cost?
options: $A_3$ idle; $A_1$ on $T_2$, $A_2$ on $T_1$; total 9
$A_2$ idle; $A_1$ on $T_2$, $A_3$ on $T_1$; total 10
$A_1$ idle; $A_2$ on $T_1$, $A_3$ on $T_2$; total 8
$A_1$ idle; $A_2$ on $T_2$, $A_3$ on $T_1$; total 14

questions.question: Agents $B_1,B_2$ and tasks $T_1,T_2,T_3$ have costs $B_1$: 4, 9, 6; $B_2$: 6, 7, 9 (for $T_1,T_2,T_3$). Each agent does one task and each task at most one agent, so a dummy agent with zero costs is added. In an optimal solution, which task is left undone and what is the total cost?
options: $T_3$ undone; total 11
$T_2$ undone; total 12
$T_1$ undone; total 13
$T_3$ undone; total 15

questions.question: An assignment problem has 3 agents and 4 tasks. Instead of adding a dummy agent, a planner deletes the task with the highest costs first. Why can this be worse?
options: Deleting a task makes the remaining table rectangular
Which task is best left undone depends on the whole plan
A dummy agent performs the deleted task at zero cost
Deleting a task changes the costs of the other tasks

questions.question: Two agents must each do exactly two of four tasks, with costs $c_{ij}$ and every task done once. How can this be made a square one-to-one assignment?
options: Add two dummy agent rows with zero costs
Add two dummy task columns with zero costs
Delete the two most expensive tasks
Give each agent two identical rows in the table

questions.question: Three agents $i$ and two tasks $j$, with binary $x_{ij}=1$ if agent $i$ does task $j$, are modelled without dummies. Which constraints match the dummy-task model?
options: $\sum_jx_{ij}=1$ for all $i$; $\sum_ix_{ij}\le1$ for all $j$
$\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for all $j$; $\sum_jx_{ij}=1$ for all $i$
$\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for all $j$; $\sum_jx_{ij}\le1$ for all $i$
$\sum_ix_{ij}\le1$ for all $j$; $\sum_jx_{ij}\le1$ for all $i$

questions.question: Agents $A_1,A_2,A_3$ and tasks $T_1,T_2$ have costs $A_1$: 7, 4; $A_2$: 5, 8; $A_3$: 6, 3 (for $T_1$, $T_2$). Each task needs one agent and each agent does at most one task. A dummy task is added, but with cost 10 for every agent instead of 0. What is the optimal solution?
options: $A_1$ still idle, with total 8
$A_1$ still idle, with total 18
$A_1$ still idle, with total 38
$A_3$ now idle, with total 19

questions.question: Two agents and three tasks are squared with a dummy agent. Unlike the course assumption, leaving task $T_j$ undone now costs a penalty $q_j$. What should the dummy agent's cost for $T_j$ be?
options: 0, as dummy entries are always zero
$q_j$, the penalty for leaving $T_j$ undone
$-q_j$, as the dummy agent saves the penalty
The largest real cost of $T_j$ plus $q_j$

questions.question: Agents $A_1,A_2,A_3$ and tasks $T_1,T_2$ have costs $A_1$: 7, 4; $A_2$: 5, 8; $A_3$: 6, 3 (for $T_1$, $T_2$). Each task needs one agent and each agent does at most one task. By mistake, a planner adds two dummy tasks and one dummy agent, all with cost 0, giving a $4\times4$ table. What does the optimum of this table do?
options: Costs 8, as in the correct model
Costs 0, leaving both tasks undone
Costs 5, leaving $T_2$ undone
Costs 3, leaving $T_1$ undone

questions.question: Agents $B_1,B_2$ and tasks $T_1,T_2,T_3$ have costs $B_1$: 4, 9, 6; $B_2$: 6, 7, 9 (for $T_1,T_2,T_3$). Each agent does one task and each task at most one agent. A dummy agent is added, but leaving a task undone now costs a penalty of 0, 0 and 4 for $T_1,T_2,T_3$. What is the optimal total cost?
options: 11, leaving $T_3$ undone
15, leaving $T_3$ undone
13, leaving $T_1$ undone
12, leaving $T_2$ undone

questions.question: Five agents and three tasks are squared with two dummy task columns $X_1,X_2$, all zero. In an optimal solution agents $A_4$ and $A_5$ take $X_1$ and $X_2$. Does it matter which of them gets $X_1$?
options: Yes: $X_1$ marks the agent that is idle first
Yes: only one of the swaps is an optimal solution
No: swapping them gives the same real plan and total
No: dummy columns are removed before solving
